purpose: Test externally grounded downside mechanisms that are structurally different from the failed drawdown, moving-average, breadth-divergence, and volatility-threshold rules without constructing a router or searching parameters.

primary_sources.title: Momentum turning points
primary_sources.finding_used: The signs of fixed 12-month slow and one-month fast time-series momentum identify bull, correction, bear, and rebound cycles; a fixed equal blend is the medium-speed strategy.

primary_sources.title: The correlation of equity and bond returns
primary_sources.finding_used: Treasury diversification can weaken when stock-bond correlation becomes positive, particularly in inflation-dominant environments.

primary_sources.title: Cross-asset signals and time series momentum
primary_sources.finding_used: Equity and bond trend information can contain cross-asset predictive information; this supports testing defensive-asset state separately from equity trend.

candidates.rule: At month end hold 100 percent SPY when the lagged 252-session return is nonnegative; otherwise hold 100 percent SHY.
At month end hold 100 percent SPY when the lagged 21-session return is nonnegative; otherwise hold 100 percent SHY.
At month end allocate equal fixed weight to the slow and fast long-flat signals, producing 100, 50, or 0 percent SPY exposure with the remainder in SHY.

Preserve the medium strategy's SPY exposure. Allocate its defensive remainder to IEF only when lagged 60-session SPY-IEF return correlation is negative and lagged 63-session IEF return is positive; otherwise choose the stronger positive lagged 63-session return of BIL or GLD, defaulting to BIL.

evaluation.recurrence: whole episodes and non-overlapping calendar blocks
evaluation.acceptance: cost-sized median episode edge, positive stress profit factor, block recurrence, family-wide Benjamini-Hochberg control, and no unacceptable whole-path opportunity cost

blocked_future_candidate.reason: requires release-time point-in-time credit-spread ingestion and an independently credible fixed rule; ETF price ratios are not an equivalent substitute
